profile.objective: Estimate reported margin and runway and identify the checks needed before relying on them.
profile.model_rationale: The case describes a subscription business. The financial table aggregates sales across customers and products.
profile.scope: Fictional annual revenue and cost figures with a reported cash balance and monthly burn.

claims.statement: Management reports USD 100,000 of revenue for the stated period.

thesis.management: Management reports annual revenue of USD 100,000.
thesis.independent: The accounts give an initial margin and runway estimate, subject to a bank and invoice reconciliation.
falsifiers: A restricted cash balance or a different normalised burn rate changes the runway estimate.

safeguards.rationale: No registration extract authenticates the legal entity or its ownership.

factors.question: Resolve legal identity, jurisdiction, ownership and instruments; distinguish operating entity from brand.
factors.finding: The registration and ownership records are missing.
factors.impact: The issuer and the holders entitled to financing proceeds are unconfirmed.
factors.next_test: Match the certificate of incorporation, shareholder register and signed financing terms.

factors.question: Test urgency, alternatives, willingness to pay and demonstrated adoption.
factors.finding: There are no buyer interviews, orders or customer-level receipts.
factors.impact: Demand at the proposed price cannot be estimated.
factors.next_test: Match purchase orders to invoices and receipts by customer.

factors.question: Assess current readiness, delivery evidence, differentiation and critical dependencies.
factors.finding: The materials contain no delivery or acceptance records.
factors.impact: The product work needed before the next sale is unknown.
factors.next_test: Inspect a delivery log and the customer’s acceptance criteria.

factors.question: Verify relevant track record, responsibilities, key-person dependency, conflicts and governance.
factors.finding: The materials give no evidence of management responsibilities or previous delivery.
factors.impact: The operating plan has no verified owner.
factors.next_test: Identify who owns delivery and check a comparable project that person led.

factors.question: Test reachable market, competitors, substitutes, channels and pricing; distinguish top-down TAM from addressable sales.
factors.finding: There are no dated offers for competing products or substitutes.
factors.impact: An attainable selling price cannot be benchmarked.
factors.next_test: Compare quotes for the same buyer, scope and effective date.

factors.question: Reconcile actual revenue and cost structure, monetisation, contribution and repeatability.
factors.finding: The company reports USD 100,000 of revenue and USD 40,000 of direct costs.
factors.impact: The implied gross margin is 60% before any adjustment to revenue recognition or cost allocation.
factors.next_test: Match recorded revenue and direct costs against invoices and supplier bills.

factors.question: Test cash availability, financing, burn, debt, working capital, runway and future funding needs.
factors.finding: The company reports USD 60,000 cash and USD 10,000 monthly burn.
factors.impact: At that burn rate, cash covers six months before restrictions, commitments or financing.
factors.next_test: Check the bank statement and reconcile the latest monthly outflow.

factors.question: Test durability of differentiation, switching costs, IP rights, scale effects and replication risks.
factors.finding: There is no record of a customer renewing, switching or choosing a competing offer.
factors.impact: The forecast has no evidence for how long customers will stay.
factors.next_test: Review renewal decisions and interview a customer that switched suppliers.

factors.question: Identify material licensing, compliance, operational, security and concentration dependencies.
factors.finding: The materials omit the agreements needed to deliver to customers.
factors.impact: A termination right or single supplier could interrupt delivery.
factors.next_test: Review the main supply and customer contracts for dependencies and termination terms.

factors.question: Identify evidence that would invalidate the thesis; determine valuation eligibility and key drivers.
factors.finding: There is no supported forecast or price for a comparable transaction.
factors.impact: The available evidence cannot establish a valuation range.
factors.next_test: Identify dated transactions and reconcile their revenue basis with the business being valued.

factors.question: Contracted recurring revenue versus bookings and one-off services; ARR bridge.
factors.finding: The records do not distinguish contracted subscriptions from one-time work.
factors.impact: Annual recurring revenue cannot be derived from total sales.
factors.next_test: Reconcile recurring invoice lines to signed prices, service periods and cancellations.

factors.question: Cohorts, GRR/NRR, churn, CAC and payback with consistent definitions.
factors.finding: There is no opening cohort, renewal history or customer acquisition spend.
factors.impact: Retention and payback cannot be estimated.
factors.next_test: Match customers across billing periods and reconcile acquisition spend to new accounts.

factors.question: Hosting and service costs, contribution, support and enterprise sales cycle.
factors.finding: Hosting and customer-support costs are not broken out.
factors.impact: The contribution from adding another account is unknown.
factors.next_test: Compare hosting, implementation and support costs by account and usage.

research.reason: The example uses only the supplied records. External sources and private confirmations were unavailable.

metrics.reason: Revenue less direct costs, divided by revenue for the same period.
Opening cash divided by reported monthly net burn, assuming that outflow continues.

challenges.finding: Unrestricted cash has no bank confirmation.
challenges.correction: Obtain the statement at the analysis date and reconcile restricted amounts before relying on runway.

gaps.item: Bank statement, restricted balances and monthly cash movements
gaps.period: At the analysis date and each month of the forecast
gaps.why: The opening balance and commitments have no independent confirmation.
gaps.conclusion: Timing and amount of the next financing.
gaps.action: Reconcile available cash and recalculate the first month below the minimum balance.

decision.conclusion: Reported gross margin is 60%, and USD 60,000 of cash covers six months at the reported burn. Confirm receipts and unrestricted cash before relying on those figures.
decision.limitations: All figures and records in this example are fictional. No outside confirmation was obtained.
strengths: The supplied figures allow the arithmetic to be reproduced.
risks: A one-month burn rate may omit irregular payments.
